parsed.process: Manual stripping of cork-oak bark with a single hand axe (machado)
parsed.process_problem: Success depends entirely on the harvester's skill; cutting too deep damages the cambium and harms the tree, larger intact sheets are worth more, and there is no labeled defect dataset of 'good vs cambium-damaging' strips.
parsed.recent_technique: Vision-language model zero-shot / few-shot anomaly detection (FADE / IADGPT / VMAD, CLIP-based prompting + in-context learning)
parsed.how_it_improves: A head-mounted or pole-cam films the exposed inner bark and the trunk surface left after each sheet is pried off. Frames go to a VLM anomaly detector prompted with text like 'exposed yellowish-pink living cambium / torn fibrous wood' vs 'clean honey-brown cork mother layer', plus 3-5 reference photos a master harvester labels in the field as good/over-cut. The model returns a localized heatmap + score flagging spots where the axe likely reached the cambium, and a coarse split/crack map on the peeled sheet. Output is a real-time 'cut depth OK / too deep here' overlay and a per-tree damage log — letting the harvester adjust pressure mid-strip and giving cooperatives an objective quality/damage grade without a per-tree trained model.
parsed.why_recent_technique_beats_mature_approa: Mature supervised defect detection (a CNN/segmentation net) needs a large labeled dataset of cambium-damaged vs clean strips per bark type — but this open problem states no such dataset exists, and creating one means deliberately wounding protected trees on a 9-year harvest cycle, which is unacceptable. The new capability is exactly that VLM zero/few-shot detectors localize anomalies on UNSEEN objects with NO labeled defect corpus, driven by natural-language descriptions of what 'damage' looks like plus a handful of in-context reference images — removing the labeled-data blocker entirely.
parsed.feasibility_now: NOT a clean drop-in. The technique is HIGH availability (open code: FADE, VMAD, IADGPT) and needs only commodity cameras, so no special hardware and no defect training set. BUT the 89.6% headline is on MVTec industrial parts; live cork bark and torn cambium are out-of-distribution natural textures with variable lighting, sap, and dust outdoors, so zero-shot transfer is plausible but unproven. Realistically it needs a field calibration pass: a few-shot reference set curated by expert harvesters and on-site validation before any score is trusted for real cut decisions — assistive flagging first, not autonomous control.
parsed.primary_quote: cutting too deep damages the cambium (harming the tree)

reasoning_trace.inputs_seen: the cork-stripping process + the open problem (no labeled good/damaging dataset, skill-dependent, cambium damage and sheet integrity drive value) + VLMAD's label-free zero/few-shot localization capability + its HIGH_avail_MEDIUM_OOD maturity tier
reasoning_trace.reasoning: The open problem's defining blocker is the explicit absence of a labeled defect dataset, and building one would require harming long-lived protected trees — so any data-hungry supervised approach is structurally blocked. VLMAD's NEW capability is anomaly localization on unseen objects from text prompts plus a few in-context references, which is precisely a label-free fit. Feasibility is realistic-not-optimistic because the cited 89.6% is on industrial MVTec objects while wet, sappy, outdoor cork bark is OOD, so I scope it as assistive + needing field calibration rather than autonomous depth control.
reasoning_trace.decision: Use a CLIP-based zero/few-shot VLM anomaly detector on head/pole-cam video of the exposed inner bark to localize and flag likely cambium over-cuts and sheet splits in near-real-time, calibrated with a small expert-curated reference set, as a harvester aid and objective damage/quality log.
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - HIGH tool availability and a genuine label-free fit, but MEDIUM because cork/cambium are OOD textures and the accuracy numbers come from industrial benchmarks.
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: Zero/few-shot transfer fails to distinguish freshly exposed living cambium from normal mother-cork tone under outdoor lighting and sap, so flags are too noisy to trust; or experts already judge depth reliably enough by eye/feel that an unproven OOD detector adds no value.
